quotes.text: These aren't technical failures, they're visibility failures. The cloud was working exactly as designed, but nobody was watching.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes surprise cloud bills as a visibility problem rather than a technical one.

quotes.text: Cost management isn't optional. It's not something you think about after you get a big bill. It's a must have practice from day one, whether you're a solo developer with a free trial or a company spending millions on Azure.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, memorable thesis that cost control starts on day one for everyone.

quotes.text: If you're not tagging your resources, you're flying blind. You might know your total bill, but you won't know which team, which project, or which environment is driving those costs.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains concisely why resource tagging is the foundation of cost allocation.

quotes.text: That's where budgets and alerts come in as your early warning system, and they're the single most important thing you can set up to avoid the horror stories we talked about earlier.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A direct recommendation naming budgets and alerts as the top priority.

quotes.text: The 80/20 rule applies here, which means 80% of your savings will come from 20% of your resources. Instead of trying to optimize everything at once, find your biggest spenders first
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical prioritization rule for where to start optimizing cloud costs.

chapters.title: What Azure Cost Management actually is
Billing hierarchy, resource hierarchy and tags
Budgets and alerts: your early warning system

takeaways: Azure Cost Management is included with every subscription and lets you monitor, analyze, control and optimize cloud spending, with cost data refreshed roughly every four hours.
Tagging resources by project, environment, cost center and owner, enforced with Azure Policy, bridges the billing and resource hierarchies so every charge can be traced to a team.

Budgets with alerts at several thresholds, plus reservations, savings plans, Azure Hybrid Benefit, auto-shutdown, right-sizing and spot instances, prevent surprise bills without sacrificing performance.
hook: Surprise Azure bills are rarely technical failures; they happen because nobody is watching idle VMs, orphaned disks and forgotten environments. This episode is for admins, developers and finance teams new to Azure, and walks through cost analysis, tags, budgets, alerts and discount options so you can set up your first budget and alert in minutes.
